body.x: Keeping track of blood sugar still usually means a finger-prick or a sensor stuck under the skin, replaced every couple of weeks. Reading it from a ring, with no needle at all, would turn a daily burden into a habit.
Nano Miracle was named a 2027 Honoree in Products in Support of Human Security for All at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for the GlucAi Ring, a non-invasive glucose monitoring ring.

GlucAi Ring is billed as the world's first AI-powered, ring-type non-invasive continuous glucose monitor, tracking blood glucose 24/7 without needles, patches or skin penetration. More than 537 million diabetics and 900 million pre-diabetics worldwide must either endure daily finger-prick pain or pay $150 to $200 monthly for minimally invasive CGM, which requires subcutaneous sensor re-insertion every 10 to 14 days and causes skin irritation, infection risk and an inherent 5-to-15-minute lag from interstitial-fluid sensing.

GlucAi Ring integrates patented multi-wavelength near-infrared spectroscopy with a proprietary ensemble machine-learning algorithm to directly measure blood glucose from finger capillaries in real time, cutting total cost of ownership by 70 percent and eliminating disposable sensors.
Its stated vision is to transform continuous glucose monitoring from a painful clinical burden into an accessible, everyday metabolic health habit for 1.4 billion people worldwide.

The CES Innovation Awards program, an annual competition honoring outstanding design and engineering in consumer technology products, recognizes all recipients as Honorees at two levels. The Honoree level covers products that score above the scoring threshold in each category, while Best of Innovation goes to the highest-scoring Honorees. A panel of industry expert judges and global media scores each product on engineering and functionality, aesthetic and design, and what makes it unique and innovative.

AVING NEWS, a global media company with 21 years of experience covering CES, operates AVING CES Newsroom (avingces.news), a dedicated platform for delivering the latest innovations to global audiences. Publishing more than 1,000 articles and conducting hundreds of on-site video interviews annually, AVING NEWS has helped Korean startups gain international visibility and expand their global reach. At CES 2027, AVING NEWS will operate the AVING TECH TALK broadcast zone at the Venetian Expo (Hall A, Booth 50271), providing on-site coverage and interviews that spotlight Korean companies and their latest innovations.
